newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bourse to abolish most trading seats.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bourse to abolish most trading seats.

text.p: The Shanghai stock exchange will use off-floor trading to replace 2,000 of the existing 3,600 trading seats on the bourse, the Shanghai Securities News on Tuesday quoted a senior exchange official as saying.
The process will be completed by the end of March next year, the newspaper quoted Liu Bo, the exchange's deputy general manager, as saying. It did not give further details.

The Shanghai exchange has come under increasing pressure from brokers in recent months to take measures to improve business and liquidity in the face of a growing challenge from Shenzhen, analysts said.

Two weeks ago, the exchange launched computerised off-floor trading after a two-month trial period. More than 100 domestic brokerages and securities branches around China have begun to use the new system to trade on the exchange, brokers said.
The exchange has said it wants off-floor trading through computer networks to become the primary means of trading on the exchange, thereby expanding its business throughout China.
It has ruled that securities offices in Shanghai only have to retain one trading seat on the bourse floor and can do the bulk of their trading through remote terminals.
In Shenzhen, off-floor trading started in July 1993 and accounts for more than 99 percent of trading volume, exchange officials have said.
